doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Law school, California and taking over a San Diego shipyard
summary: After the bar exam he became an assistant to a banker, found the shipyard treasurer stealing, and ended up running it.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: So you came back from the service and went to law school.
I went here, and then to law school, and then right to California.
Did the business that you got into, was it serendipitous somehow? How did that actually happen?

Well I went to California. I studied the summer in June of ’49. I studied for the bar, took the bar in November, October, and went looking for a job. And all the law firms said yeah we love you, you look great, you went to a good school, and when you pass the bar come on back. Well I had a wife and a child and a pregnant wife at that. And I needed some dough. So I heard of a guy, a big guy in town who needed an administrative assistant with legal training, so I thought well I’ll try that. So I went to see him and I got the job and I went to work for this fella, who owned a bank and a bunch of other stuff in town. And I worked for him for a year or so and then one of the things he owned was a little shipyard. And somebody was stealing from the shipyard, so he called me and asked me would I go down to the shipyard and sign on as assistant treasurer and see if I could find out who it was. I said okay, but remember I don’t want to stay there, I want to come back to the bank. I want to be uptown. Because I was still thinking I was going to practice. And I was right in the middle of everybody who was anybody in town. I had every connection there could possibly be in this little town. Anyway I went down as assistant treasurer and the first day I discovered that the crook was the treasurer.
The first day you discovered that?

The first day, yeah. So I reported that, and then I had to stay on as treasurer you see. And I stayed for five or six months I guess, and I got very upset because the company wasn’t doing anything and the management stunk and there was no future, you know, nothing. So I quit. And I resigned, and that night he came out to my house and talked me into coming back to run the shipyard. So I did. And I had a hell of a time.
That’s an amazing leap for a young man.
Yeah, my objective incidentally was to make that as good a shipyard as could be, but to build a submarine. That was my objective. Never made it.
Wow. Ship building is a whole amazing field.
We could spend hours on that.
